name: Rabbit Care Checklist
description: A rabbit care checklist covering housing, a hay-based diet, litter, grooming and health.

items.text: Provide a large enclosure or rabbit-proofed pen
Allow daily time to run and stretch in a safe area
items.note: Rabbits need exercise well beyond a small hutch

items.text: Add a hideout or covered area for security
Keep housing out of extreme heat, cold and drafts
Use solid flooring or soft surfaces to protect feet
Offer unlimited fresh grass hay at all times
Provide a variety of rabbit-safe leafy greens daily
Give a small measured portion of quality pellets
Limit treats and avoid sugary or starchy foods
Supply clean, fresh water daily in a bowl or bottle
Set up a litter box with rabbit-safe litter and hay
Spot-clean the litter box daily
Clean the full enclosure and replace bedding regularly
Wash food and water containers
Check corners for soiling outside the box
Brush the coat regularly, more often during molts
items.note: Rabbits ingest loose fur when self-grooming

items.text: Check and trim nails as needed
Inspect the rear end for soiling, especially in warm weather
Check ears and eyes for discharge or irritation
Never bathe a rabbit unless advised by a vet
Watch appetite and droppings daily for changes
items.note: A rabbit not eating or pooping needs urgent vet care

items.text: Check teeth alignment and watch for drooling
Observe behavior, posture and energy levels
Feel for lumps or signs of pain during handling
Schedule routine check-ups with a rabbit-savvy vet
Provide chew toys to support dental health
Offer tunnels, boxes and digging or foraging options
Spend daily time interacting at floor level
Consider a bonded companion, as rabbits are social
Rotate toys to keep the environment interesting

faq.a: Unlimited grass hay should make up most of a rabbit's diet, supported by fresh leafy greens, a small measured portion of pellets and limited treats. Constant hay supports digestion and wears down continuously growing teeth.

faq.q: How much space does a pet rabbit need?
faq.a: Rabbits need far more room than a small hutch — a large enclosure plus daily time to run and stretch in a safe, rabbit-proofed area. Confinement to a tiny cage harms their health and behavior.

faq.q: Can rabbits use a litter box?
faq.a: Yes. Many rabbits litter-train well, especially once spayed or neutered. Place a litter box with rabbit-safe litter and a handful of hay in their favored corner and clean it regularly.

faq.q: When should I take my rabbit to a vet?
faq.a: Rabbits hide illness, so see a rabbit-savvy vet for any drop in appetite or droppings, which can signal a serious gut problem. This checklist is general guidance; routine check-ups and spay or neuter are best discussed with a vet.

faq.q: Can I print this rabbit care checklist?
faq.a: Yes. Print it or download the PDF so you can keep it handy and tick off daily and routine tasks.
